summary: Mabel Haynes Bode was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Bern and studied at institutions including UCL, Paris, and Pisa. She taught at UCL (1909, 1911–1917) and SOAS (1917).

Madan Mohan Malaviya worked in Indology and other fields. After studying at Muir Central College, the University of Calcutta, and the University of Allahabad, he founded Banaras Hindu University in 1916 and served as its Vice Chancellor from 1919 to 1938.

Madeleine Biardeau was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at ENS de Sèvres, the University of Kerala, and under K. A. Sivaramakrishna Sastri. She served as Professor of Indian Religions at EPHE from circa 1956 to 1989.

Madeleine Giteau specialized in Buddhist studies and archaeology, earning degrees from EPHE and Sorbonne Nouvelle University. She served at the National Museum of Cambodia, École française d'Extrême-Orient, and as Professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1981–1985).

Madeleine Hallade was an art historian and archaeologist who studied at the École des Beaux-Arts and École du Louvre. She served as Chargée de Mission at the Guimet Museum (1935–1965) and Chargé de Conferences at the École du Louvre (circa 1945–1965).

Madhav M. Deshpande is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fergusson College and the University of Pennsylvania under scholars including George Cardona and Shivram Dattatray Joshi. He served as Professor at the University of Michigan from 1972 to 2017.

Madhav Sadashiv Gore studied at the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and at the Columbia University School of Social Work. He later held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University from circa 1997 to 2002.

Madhu Khanna is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. Her career includes posts at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts and as Director at Jamia Millia Islamia in 2012.

Madhu Parameswaran is a scholar in Indology and archaeology who completed an MD (Ayu) at Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (2007–2010). He served as an Assistant Professor at Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier Ayurveda College starting in 2011.

Madhura Balasubramaniam is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD in 2022 at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, where she previously served as a Project Associate from 2018 to 2020.

Madhusudan Amilal Dhaky was an Indologist and art historian who studied at Fergusson College and founded the Archeology Research Group in Porbandar in 1951. He served as Associate Director and Director Emeritus of Research at the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Madhusudan Gupta was an Indologist and medical scholar who studied at Sanskrit College and Calcutta Medical College. He held teaching posts at Sanskrit College (~1830–1835) and Calcutta Medical College (~1835–1856).
Madhusudan Kaul Shastri was an Indologist who served as Superintendent of the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir, attested during 1918–1934 and 1943–1945.
Madhusudan Rimal is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Alberta in 2016 and held a post there in 2021.
Madhusudan Singh Vats was an archaeologist and Indologist who succeeded Rakhal Das Banerji.

Magdalena Szpindler is an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Warsaw and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań. In 2019, she held an Adiunkt position at the University of Warsaw.

Magdalene Geiger was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, studying under Wilhelm Geiger, Hermann Beckh, and Heinrich Lüders.
Magdalene Sophie Schott was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at multiple German universities, completing her Ph.D. under Max Walleser at Heidelberg University in 1935.

Maggie Bickford is a sinologist and art historian who studied at Bennington College, Yale University, and Princeton University. She served as Professor of East Asian Studies at Brown University in 1993 and was a Member at the Institute for Advanced Study.

Mahadev Govind Ranade was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Elphinstone College, the University of Mumbai, and Government Law College, Mumbai. He founded the Maharashtra Girls Education Society in 1885.
